Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

understand verb

also realise, realize, grasp, do you understand now?, got it?, do you follow?, now I see, I see, I get it, get the point?, I don’t understand

classical

Ter. And. 348: Obtundis, tametsī intellegō.
Traupman 32
Traupman 26: quid dīcās ego nōn intellegō, I don’t understand what you are saying

intellegō, intellegere, intellēxī, intellēctum

verb, third conjugation

understand, realise

With an accusative, an accusative and infinitive (realise that), or a question: Num tū intellegis hīc quid narret? (Ter. Ph. 846). Nōn satis intellegō: I don’t quite understand (Traupman 110). Lewis & Short calls intelligō “less correct”.

Other words

  • teneō, tenēre, tenuī, tentum — grasp, follow (what is said)

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Heaut. 4.3.22: tenēs, quid dīcam? (Lewis & Short s.v. teneō); Plaut. Capt. 3.5.39: nunc ego teneō, nunc sciō (Lewis & Short); Traupman 110: jam tenēs?; Traupman 29

    “To hold” what is said, as English “grasp”: Tenēs?, do you follow?

  • teneō, tenēre, tenuī — I see, I get it, I follow

    verb, second conjugation: teneō, I’ve got it; tenēsne?, do you follow? · also used · classical · Plaut. Poen. 3.5.23: hahahae, jam teneō, quid sit (Lewis & Short s.v. ha); Traupman 107: now I see (I understand), jam teneō; Traupman 105: get the point?, tenēsne (pl. tenētisne) rem?

    “To hold” the point, as English “grasp”: jam teneō, now I’ve got it.

Examples

  • Num tū intellegis hīc quid narret? — Num tū? — Nihil. — Tantundem ego.

    Do you understand what he’s saying? — Do you? — Not a thing. — Nor do I.Ter. Ph. 846

  • quārē nōn, ut intellegere possit, sed, nē omnīnō possit nōn intellegere, cūrandum

    so we must take care not that he can understand, but that he cannot possibly fail to understandQuint. 8.2.24

  • avāritia vērō senīlis quid sibi velit, nōn intellegō

    but what an old man’s greed is for, I do not understandCic. Sen. 65

  • ō mē īnfēlīcem! quī nunc dēmum intellegō ūtilia mihi quam fuerint quae dēspexeram

    poor me! only now do I realise how useful to me were the things I had despisedPhaedr. 1.12.13–14

  • Jam tenēs?

    Do you understand now?Traupman 110

See also I get it!, do you get it?, mean, hear, speak.
